sentences.text: Stegosaurus is a quadrupedal dinosaur identified by a double row of vertical kite-shaped plates on its back and two pairs of horizontal spikes at the tail's end.
The animal is characterized by these upright plates along its back and spikes located on its tail.
The type species, S. stenops, measured 6.5 meters long with a mass of 3.5 metric tons, while S. ungulatus measured 7 meters long with a mass of 3.8 metric tons.
Some large individuals may have reached lengths of 7.5 to 9 meters and masses of 5.0 to 5.3 metric tons.
The genus Stegosaurus was described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1877.
Marsh initially identified these remains during the Bone Wars at Dinosaur Ridge National Landmark.
The first remains were discovered by Arthur Lakes and H.C. Beckwith in Quarry 5 north of Morrison, Colorado, consisting of caudal vertebrae, a dermal plate, and other postcranial elements.
Remains of over 80 individual Stegosaurus animals have been discovered since then.
Due to its short neck and small head, Stegosaurus likely fed on low-lying bushes and shrubs.
It is generally agreed that Stegosaurus used its spiked tails for defense and its plates primarily for display, with secondary thermoregulatory functions.
A large spike preserved in Stegosaurus sulcatus has been speculated to be a shoulder spike used for species diagnosis.
The type species of the genus Stegosaurus is Stegosaurus stenops.
Two other species within the genus are Stegosaurus ungulatus, described in 1879, and Stegosaurus sulcatus, described in 1887.
Hypsirhophus and Diracodon have been proposed as synonyms for Stegosaurus.
Stegosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic period, specifically from the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages.
Stegosaurus fossils have been found in the western United States and Portugal, dating between 155 and 145 million years ago.
A Stegosaurus specimen from Portugal was originally thought to belong to the Alcobaça Formation but was later suggested to be from the Lourinhã Formation.
Marsh initially hypothesized that Stegosaurus was an aquatic, turtle-like animal and believed its plates lay flat over its back like roof shingles.
Analysis has revealed that the holotype specimen of Stegosaurus armatus is dubious, leading to the replacement of the type species.
While many researchers consider Hypsirhophus a synonym of Stegosaurus, Peter Galton (2010) suggested it is distinct based on vertebral differences.
Four different arrangements for the back plates of Stegosaurus have been proposed throughout history.
